newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela aluminium debt to be partly securitized.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela aluminium debt to be partly securitized.

text.p: Some 20 percent of the $600 million in debt that aluminium companies in Venezuela's Corporacion Venezolana de Guyana (CVG) currently hold with the government will be securitized, government officials said.

The rest will be restructured over a three- to five-year period, Venezuelan Investment Fund President Alberto Poletto told reporters. The restructuring is an attempt to boost the sale price of the companies, due to be privatised in Janaury.

"Extending the debt profile is a better option than selling the companies with a deceptively attractive debt restructuring," he said. The securitized debt will meanwhile be placed on the market as two-year bonds, he said.
The plan is the latest attempt to restructure the companies' $1.26 billion in commercial and government debt.
However, any restructuring of the remaining $660 million in commercial debt will be between the new owner of the aluminium companies and their creditor banks, Poletto added.
